trust_decision.summary: A caller-supplied file path is trusted: the Jira attachment upload (reached from jira_update_issue's 'attachments' argument) and the Confluence attachment upload / page 'content_file' readers pass the string to open()/read_text with only an existence check, so any tool caller can read any file the server can read and push it into Jira/Confluence content (confused deputy).

landing_point.why: The advisory names jira update_issue, so the first look is the tool's 'attachments' parameter, whose file paths are parsed at :1897-1922 and handed to JiraFetcher.update_issue.

fix_sites.entry_point: every Confluence tool (client construction in ConfluenceFetcher.__init__)
every Jira tool (client construction in JiraFetcher.__init__)
every tool via get_jira_fetcher/get_confluence_fetcher (unauthenticated HTTP global-credential fallback)
MCP tools/list and tools/call over streamable-http (enablement + read-only enforcement)
SSLIgnoreAdapter used when SSL verification is disabled (all clients)
all HTTP sessions (mounted by both client initialisers)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about JIRA update_issue, and Confluence has its own separate upload method in another package whose download half already calls validate_safe_path - so it reads as a different feature that is already protected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Relative and absolute paths that stay inside the workspace must keep working: the attachment uploads implement relative->absolute resolution, and Confluence content_file is documented as accepting absolute or relative paths. Rejecting relative paths, or any write under the CWD, breaks documented behaviour (the fix had to move its own e2e fixtures into a CWD subdirectory).

O6_input_shapes: absolute path outside the workspace (e.g. /etc/passwd, or a sibling of CWD)
list of paths (Confluence file_paths, jira upload_attachments)
content_file argument with ~ expansion, passed as str or Path
symlink whose target escapes the workspace (validate_safe_path resolves symlinks)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ConfluenceFetcher.download_attachment(url, target_path) writes the response next to the same workspace check but without the CWD-root refusal the fix adds to the Jira twin, so a download can overwrite an importable module in the working-directory root (write half of the same path-confinement contract).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the fix comment talk about JIRA downloads, and this method already calls validate_safe_path, so it looks finished.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sibling package confluence/ vs jira/, one package over

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ConfluenceFetcher.download_content_attachments(content_id, target_dir) writes every attachment into a caller-chosen directory, also with no CWD-root refusal.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The MCP tool of the same name takes no target_dir (it returns embedded resources), so this helper looks unreachable and thus untouched by any tool-level fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sibling package confluence/ vs jira/, one package over

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a 'content_file' / 'description_file' argument on jira_create_issue that reads the body from disk
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Confluence create_page/update_page already take content_file, the Jira create tool has the symmetric description argument, and this project copies such parameters across the two services.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third upload path that opens the file itself instead of delegating to upload_attachment (a path-taking variant beside _upload_attachment_from_bytes)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same file already carries two upload transports (_upload_attachment_direct for paths, _upload_attachment_from_bytes for bytes), so adding a path-reading sibling is a natural refactor that would bypass the fix site.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an 'attachments' kwarg on create_issue reusing upload_attachments
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: update_issue already accepts attachments here and the create/update pair is kept symmetric throughout jira/issues.py.
